whatThisVerdictIsNot: It is not a finding that the rendering is wrong. Geometry, fit, refusals, ink, protected-field treatment, flattening, sanitation, field census, classification and visual output were re-derived from the real bytes and all reproduce correctly. Both corrections are about the artifacts being stale against the canonical factory, and about the provenance sidecar not meeting the contract the platform claims to enforce.
methodNote: node_modules is not installed in this clone, so scripts/verify-rcap-shared-pdf-contract.mjs cannot run (pdf-lib is absent). Every PDF-level finding below was derived by direct byte inspection of the committed artifacts and by reading the factory source at HEAD, rather than by re-running the lane's own verifier. For an independent review that is the stronger method: the lane's verifier is not asked to grade itself.

participantValueVisibility.weaknessInTheEvidenceChain: The finalized-artifact audit normalizes markers by stripping whitespace and lowercasing, so its marker 'Example County' matches 'examplecounty'. The round-2 defect it was meant to catch ('Example County        COUNTY') also contains that substring. That audit line cannot discriminate the fix from the defect it replaced. Benign here only because the value was confirmed directly from the content stream and the raster.

longNameFixture.observed: A 69-character name is refused on Defendant's Name at value_exceeds_widget_width_at_minimum_font, and written at 6.5pt on Name Printed or Typed, which is wider. Both correct.
longNameFixture.fragility: The refusal clears by under 1pt (required ~195.6-196.1 against 195.11 usable). Any change to horizontal padding or font metrics flips it. Not a defect; worth knowing before touching either.

longAddressFixture.observed: Refused at the 6pt floor (required ~214.7 against 213.11 usable), left blank, with a recorded participant fallback.

captionFixture.observed: COUNTY suffix normalization works and is recorded: 'Example County' writes 'Example', and the boundary value writes at 7pt and stops clear of both the rule end and the printed word COUNTY. No doubling. The boundary Case No. is refused rather than run into the caption divider. The trailing-whitespace defect from round 3 is fixed at HEAD.

finalPage.observed: Source 1 page; both fixtures 1 page at 612x792; contact sheet 1 page. No page added or lost.
finalPage.staleClaimInTheRecord: overlay-profile.json declares overflowPolicy.longText 'shrink_to_fit_then_addendum', but no addendum is implemented or produced anywhere in the factory. The real behaviour is shrink to the 6pt floor then refuse with a recorded manual fallback, which refusalFallbacks describes correctly. The overflowPolicy line is a stale claim inside the file that serves as the review record.

rasterizedVisualEvidence.observed: The contact sheet raster was read directly: left panel blank, right panel carries all six participant values on their rules, with Signature, Email, Telephone, Date and State Bar No. left blank and no value overlapping a preprinted caption.
rasterizedVisualEvidence.caveat: contact-sheet-visual-proof.json records controlDiscriminates null for this sheet — a one-page sheet has no second page to serve as a known-different control, so the pixel measurement's discriminating power is unproven for this sheet specifically. The content-stream proof and the direct read of the raster are the stronger evidence and both hold.

packetFamilyMapping.observed: Track wi_exp_cr266 requires two families: WI:cr-266-form-en as primary filing (this one, technical_approved) and WI:cr-267-form-en as proposed order. CR-267's source is not in this clone, it has zero anchors derived, and it is held awaiting a Case No. placement decision. So the packet is not assemblable. CR-266's own mapping is exact and clean.

familyLocalWorkarounds.observed: printedSuffixAfterBlank, protectedRules, deliberatelyUnbound, expectedOutcome and approvedTextColor are all parameters consumed by the shared factory. The WI package supplies data, not behaviour. No shadow renderer, no per-family override, no local reimplementation of shared behaviour.

corrections.page: document level — the PDF Info dictionary, not a page
corrections.actualResult: D:20260101000000Z — both dates pinned to the deterministic stamp, which is what the pre-canonical factory did.
corrections.requiredResult: The source's own creation date, D:20240624114823-05'00'. At HEAD, carryDates() sets CreationDate from the source document and only ModDate to the deterministic stamp (scripts/rcap-official-forms/rcap-official-form-finalize.mjs:142-152, called at :308).
corrections.whyThisMatters: The approved artifacts are not what the canonical factory at HEAD produces. Re-rendering changes the Info dict, therefore the bytes, therefore every artifact SHA. The platform-ready gate re-hashes each file named by the round-4 approval and fails when one has moved, so the first time the lane runs its own renderer on HEAD this asset falls out of platform_ready. The round-4 approval names a pre-merge head.
corrections.smallestCorrection: Run the flat-overlay family renderer on HEAD, then re-take the round-4 approval against the new bytes and update reviewedArtifactSha256 and reviewedHead. The approval must be re-taken, not transcribed: the bytes under review changed.
corrections.failingFixture: node scripts/render-rcap-flat-overlay-families.mjs --check — the drift gate the handoff workflow already runs
corrections.verifiedIndependently: Yes. The committed canonical fixture carries /CreationDate (D:20260101000000Z) and /ModDate (D:20260101000000Z); the source carries /CreationDate(D:20240624114823-05'00'); HEAD's carryDates sets creation from the source and only modification to the stamp.
